messages:
Morgan (eng-platform): thinking out loud: what if instead of slow ramping traffic weights we do a 'shadow + probe + gated-cut' approach: shadow 100% non-blocking, run stratified probes for latency/quality, then flip weights only when probes + mirrors are green. thoughts?
June (architecture): sounds reasonable. key is making shadows truly non-intrusive. also need clear decision boundary for automatic cutback.
Alex (eng-runtime): +1 on non-intrusive. runtime plan: mirrors go to a best-effort path that never queues on the critical GPU queue. use a bounded buffer and drop if full. tag mirrored requests with X-Shadow: true.
Iris (eng-sre): probe cadence matters. If probes are too sparse we miss intermittent regressions. propose adaptive probing: baseline 1r/min per variant, double on anomaly, and sample more during traffic spikes.
Dee (eng-ml): sampling must be stratified by sequence length and function-calls vs chat. Also include a tiny canary corpus of representative prompts for semantic checks. 
Morgan (eng-platform): config sketch I'm imagining: 
```
experiment:
  mirror: { enabled: true, priority: best-effort, max_buffer: 500 }
  probes:
    - name: short
      rate: 1r/min
    - name: long
      rate: 0.2r/min
  auto_fallback:
    latency_threshold_pct: 99
    latency_multiplier: 1.35
    error_rate_threshold: 0.02
    evaluation_check: semantic_epsilon: 0.05
```
June (architecture): automatic fallback behavior needs two safeguards: 1) preconditions (fallback target has capacity + cost check), 2) observability annotations so teams see why fallback occurred.
Alex (eng-runtime): runtime note: fallback should be enacted as a routing policy that can be reversed quickly. implement as weight override with TTL and an audit event. Also preserve session affinity when switching so ongoing conversations aren't split.
Iris (eng-sre): add a canary-rollback safety: when fallback happens, trigger a lightweight health-check against the previous variant to see if rollback is safe, and don't escalate to incident until both checks fail.
Dee (eng-ml): quality signal: run NLL/embedding-drift on the canary corpus; if combined quality delta > epsilon prefer routing back to verified model. we should not let latency-only rules destroy quality.
deploy-bot: probe/short: ok; probe/long: ok; mirror pipeline: deployed to staging
Morgan (eng-platform): action items: 1) Alex prototype bounded non-blocking mirror + header tagging 2) Dee prepare canary prompt set + drift checks 3) Iris draft adaptive probe policy + escalation rules 4) June draft lightweight RFC for config semantics and runbook snippets
June (architecture): also include a developer opt-out flag so devs can disable auto-fallback per-route while they debug. annotation must show route-level override.
Morgan (eng-platform): will add `auto_fallback: disable` override to runbook. ok if I open a follow-up thread with config examples? :thumbsup:
Iris (eng-sre): :thumbsup: also add a metric spike gate for token-cost so we don't fall back into a more expensive variant by mistake.
Alex (eng-runtime): noted. we'll emit fallback_reason and fallback_cost_delta in the audit event.
Morgan (eng-platform): thanks all, i'll draft the RFC this week and loop in infra for capacity gating.
